source_facts.fact: There are 20 SMPs covering the English coast and they set planned approaches to flood and coastal erosion risk through 2105.
source_facts.gate: SMP approach is strategic direction and not guaranteed funding or a parcel permission.

source_facts.fact: The new national coastal erosion risk map provides projections to 2055 and 2105 under scenarios with and without delivery of current shoreline management plans.
source_facts.gate: Modelled erosion bands are not exact parcel loss dates.

source_facts.fact: PPG defines CCMAs as plan areas likely to be affected by physical coastal change such as erosion, landslip, inundation or accretion.
source_facts.gate: CCMA status is a planning policy designation, not automatic refusal or proof of loss.

source_facts.fact: The national Planning Data CCMA dataset currently shows 0 records, 0 providers and no collector attempt, with MHCLG-created origin pending authoritative replacement.
source_facts.gate: Zero service records are NO_DATA, not proof no CCMA exists locally.

source_facts.fact: Environment Agency Version 2.0 coastal modelling standards were published 8 May 2026 for non-real-time open coast models.
source_facts.gate: Model standard compliance is not a parcel risk measurement or planning approval.

source_facts.fact: The 2024 national assessment uses updated NaFRA and NCERM and accounts for UKCP18 climate projections.
source_facts.gate: National risk assessment is screening evidence and not a parcel-specific engineering conclusion.

core_rules: SMP management approach is strategic direction not planning permission
SMP hold-the-line policy is not guaranteed future funding
SMP no-active-intervention is not an exact parcel loss date
managed realignment is not automatic acquisition of every affected parcel
advance-the-line policy is not evidence works have been built
SMP policy unit boundary is not a cadastral title boundary
SMP plan horizon must retain its time period
SMP updates can change management approach and must be date-checked
NCERM projection is modelled risk not a surveyed property boundary
NCERM medium-term band is not a prediction of exact erosion year
NCERM long-term band is not a guaranteed loss event
NCERM scenario with SMP delivery is not proof defences will be funded
NCERM scenario without future works is not current operational policy
areas mainly at sea-flood risk may lack erosion projections and must not be classed no-risk
CCMA is a planning designation not automatic refusal
CCMA does not prove a parcel will be lost to erosion
CCMA absence from Planning Data does not prove absence in an adopted local plan
Planning Data CCMA zero records must remain NO_DATA
local plan and adopted policies remain authoritative for local CCMA status
CCMA may be defined where significant shoreline change is expected over 100 years
hold-or-advance policy does not always remove the need for CCMA where delivery funding is uncertain
essential infrastructure may be considered in a CCMA subject to policy tests
temporary development policy in a CCMA is not permanent development permission
rollback or relocation policy is not a compulsory-purchase outcome
coastal erosion risk and coastal flooding risk must remain distinct
coastal erosion map is not a flood-depth map
flood map for planning is not a coastal erosion projection
coastal landslip requires its own evidence and must not be inferred from erosion band alone
permanent inundation and accretion are separate coastal-change processes
coastal modelling standard is not a site model
model quality guidance is not a planning decision
UKCP18 allowance use is not proof of a particular parcel outcome
national risk assessment is screening evidence not a site-specific FRA
national property-at-risk counts must not be downscaled to a parcel
FCERM strategy is national policy not a site funding award
FCERM project funding guidance is not evidence a local scheme is funded
grant-in-aid eligibility is not an approved grant
coastal erosion assistance grant eligibility is not automatic entitlement
grant availability is not proof a property will be demolished
nature-based solution policy is not evidence a scheme exists on site
saltmarsh or habitat opportunity is not a delivered defence
coastal habitat creation can interact with planning and environmental consents that remain separate
marine planning and terrestrial planning must remain coordinated but distinct
SMP adoption is not a marine licence
historic SMP document must not override current Explorer updates
NO_DATA must not be converted into no coastal-change risk
no parcel erosion date defence funding planning outcome or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
research-source confidence must not be reported as parcel coastal-risk accuracy
